expectations.text: Distinguishes PCA from EFA — states they are fundamentally different analyses (PCA models total variance; EFA models common/latent variance attributed to latent factors)
expectations.evidence: PCA models total variance. Each component is a weighted linear combination of all observed items... EFA (common factor analysis) models common variance only. It separates variance that is shared among items (attributable to latent factors) from variance that is unique to each item (specific + error). Item variance decomposes as σ² = h² (communality) + u² (uniqueness).

expectations.text: Does not endorse using PCA components as subscales for a latent-variable measurement model without flagging this limitation
expectations.evidence: interpreting PCA components as subscales for a latent-variable measurement model is a category error... do not present its components as subscales in a measurement model without flagging this loudly.

expectations.text: Warns that varimax (orthogonal) rotation is inappropriate when constructs are expected to be correlated — recommends oblique rotation instead
expectations.evidence: Varimax is an orthogonal rotation: it mathematically constrains the resulting factors/components to be uncorrelated with each other. That is almost never the right assumption for psychological constructs... Use an oblique rotation instead — promax or oblimin.

expectations.text: Warns against or questions the eigenvalue > 1 rule for selecting the number of components/factors
expectations.evidence: Kaiser's eigenvalue-greater-than-1 criterion is a convenient heuristic from 1960 that is known to systematically overestimate the number of factors/components, often badly. It has no principled statistical justification.

expectations.text: Recommends EFA with oblique rotation and polychoric correlations as the appropriate analysis for developing subscales from Likert items
expectations.evidence: fa(your_data, nfactors = 3, fm = 'minres', rotate = 'oblimin', cor = 'poly') ... polychoric correlations for Likert items ... uses an appropriate correlation matrix for ordinal data, and allows subscales to correlate as they likely do.

expectations.text: Does not simply validate the advisor's PCA recommendation without raising the PCA vs. EFA distinction
expectations.evidence: Not quite — there are three substantive problems with this approach, and I'd push back on your advisor's recommendation as stated.
